title: My computer is slow
description: Work through these steps in order — most slow-computer problems are solved by step 3.

items.hint: A full restart (Start → Power → Restart) clears memory and stops things quietly running in the background. Try this first.

items.text: Check if Windows Update is running in the background
items.hint: Click Start → Settings → Windows Update. If it shows "Downloading…" or "Installing…" that's why it's slow. Let it finish, then restart.

items.text: Check if the main drive is nearly full
items.hint: Open the Disk Report in PC Helper. A full drive (over 90%) can make the computer very slow.

items.text: Check what's starting up with Windows
items.hint: Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager. Click "Startup apps." Anything you don't recognize that's Enabled can be right-clicked and Disabled.
Click Start → Settings → Privacy & Security → Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Quick scan.

items.text: Check if the computer is hot
items.hint: Feel the bottom of the laptop or the back of the desktop. If very hot, let it cool down with vents unobstructed. Dust inside can cause overheating.
